painting.title: THE STANDING STONES ON THE MOOR AT NIGHT
painting.intro: A ring of old leaning grey stones on a low rise of short turf, high on the open moor, with a bare track running through it from left to right. It is night, clear and still, lit only by the moon.
bullets: The ground: one flat level of short, wind-cropped turf, worn pale and trodden inside the ring. A bare earth track comes in from the left edge, crosses the ring and runs out to the right edge. The pale area is open, with nothing overhanging it.

Far back, behind the ring: the dark band is heather falling away down the slope. The cone at the far left is a low outcrop of weathered rock, and the cone at the far right is a single wind-bent thorn tree, bare and black.

The far arc of the ring: four rough granite standing stones of different heights, each leaning a different way. They are lichen-spotted and weather-worn, set in the turf at the back edge of the pale ground.
Left side: one more leaning stone stands on the far side of the track where it enters the ring. Opposite it on the near side is a knee-high broken stump of a stone.

Right side: the two tallest stones stand as a gateway either side of the track. The far one is broad and almost four metres high, the near one slimmer and a little shorter. The bare track passes plainly between them and on to the right edge.
Near side of the ring: a long grey stone lies fallen flat in the turf, half sunk and mossy along its top. A low leaning stone stands to its right.

Behind the fallen stone, toward the viewer: waist-high thickets of dark gorse. Just right of the stone's end is a narrow gap where a thin bare path slips down between the bushes to the bottom edge, with a faint cold shine low in the gap.
Near corners: dark heather, low and rough, falling away from the rise on both sides.

Light: cold silver moonlight from the upper left, with soft shadows from each stone falling toward the lower right. There are no lanterns or fires; the stones' pale lit edges and the pale turf stand out against the dark moor.
painting.top: A clear night sky full of stars over the moor, which rolls away in low dark ridges to a faint horizon. Auros, the moon, is large, pale and nearly full in the upper left.

checks: "second tallest stone, near side of the road" (3.4 m tall) hides about 3 square metres of walkable ground behind it.
